b60b79b1.text: Jo has no home. He sweeps a street crossing for coins, and whenever he stops, a constable tells him to move on.
b60b79b1.spoken: Jo has no home. He sweeps a street crossing for coins, and whenever he stops, a constable tells him to move on.

3ab933de.text: And you've just started at your county's health department. This morning, a child at Riverside Elementary was diagnosed with measles.

5e2920b1.text: First, a scene from 1853. Jo sleeps in Tom-all-Alone's, a fever-ridden slum the city has left to rot. He falls sick, and Esther and Charley bring him home. Charley catches the fever from him, and Esther catches it nursing Charley. Dickens warns that the slum's disease shall work its retribution through every order of society. Now jump to December 2014. Visitors caught measles at Disneyland in California. By April 2015, it had reached a hundred and forty-seven people in seven states, with more cases in Mexico and Canada. Disease doesn't stay where it starts. So a choice about it is never only about the person who makes it.

8ec43479.text: And the one acting is usually the government, which can make rules backed by law.

091714a2.text: The epidemiologist Geoffrey Rose noticed a puzzle. A measure that prevents a lot of disease in a population often does little for each person who takes part. He called it the prevention paradox.

d97d27ee.text: When enough people are immune, a disease can't find enough new people to infect, and outbreaks die out. That's herd immunity.
d97d27ee.spoken: When enough people are immune, a disease can't find enough new people to infect, and outbreaks die out. That's herd immunity.

6f6e8fa4.text: It protects people who can't be vaccinated, like babies too young for their first dose and children in cancer treatment. They depend on everyone else.
6f6e8fa4.spoken: It protects people who can't be vaccinated, like babies too young for their first dose and children in cancer treatment. They depend on everyone else.

0cee5756.text: Measles is one of the most contagious diseases there is. Health agencies aim for at least ninety-five in a hundred children to have both doses of the vaccine.

59d7edb7.text: Good. Now for a harder question. Is there a duty to vaccinate?
59d7edb7.spoken: Good. Now for a harder question. Is there a duty to vaccinate?

e95ee021.text: Back to 1853. Charley caught the fever from Jo after helping Esther bring him home. Nobody asked her whether she'd take that risk. Today, a six-year-old in cancer treatment can't have the measles vaccine. If she catches measles at school, she never chose that risk either. So here's the question. When your choice puts a risk on people who never agreed to it, do you have a duty to choose differently? Three arguments say yes.
e95ee021.spoken: Back to 1853. Charley caught the fever from Jo after helping Esther bring him home. Nobody asked her whether she'd take that risk. Today, a six-year-old in cancer treatment can't have the measles vaccine. If she catches measles at school, she never chose that risk either. So here's the question. When your choice puts a risk on people who never agreed to it, do you have a duty to choose differently? Three arguments say yes.

1a80b0ec.text: The first argument comes from John Stuart Mill.
1a80b0ec.spoken: The first argument comes from John Stuart Mill.

43c0927b.text: Mill's harm principle says society may limit your freedom only to stop you from harming others.
43c0927b.spoken: Mill's harm principle says society may limit your freedom only to stop you from harming others.

9724a15d.text: Measles can cause pneumonia, brain swelling, and death. A child who catches it can pass it to someone who couldn't be protected.
9724a15d.spoken: Measles can cause pneumonia, brain swelling, and death. A child who catches it can pass it to someone who couldn't be protected.

22d77641.text: So refusing a vaccine isn't only about yourself. And a vaccine rule is the kind of rule the harm principle allows.
22d77641.spoken: So refusing a vaccine isn't only about yourself. And a vaccine rule is the kind of rule the harm principle allows.

1be36098.text: Here's the worry, though. One unvaccinated child adds only a tiny risk. Does a tiny risk count as harm?
1be36098.spoken: Here's the worry, though. One unvaccinated child adds only a tiny risk. Does a tiny risk count as harm?

4d24b6fd.text: The second argument is about fairness.
4d24b6fd.spoken: The second argument is about fairness.

d2657fb0.text: The philosopher Angus Dawson points out that herd immunity is a public good. Everyone nearby gets the benefit, whether or not they helped make it.
d2657fb0.spoken: The philosopher Angus Dawson points out that herd immunity is a public good. Everyone nearby gets the benefit, whether or not they helped make it.

99d6c5f5.text: A free rider takes the benefit and leaves the cost to others. Here, the cost is a sore arm and a very small risk of side effects.
99d6c5f5.spoken: A free rider takes the benefit and leaves the cost to others. Here, the cost is a sore arm and a very small risk of side effects.

a4ec3c17.text: Alberto Giubilini goes further. Protecting everyone is a shared job, and fairness says that each person who can should do their fair share of it.
a4ec3c17.spoken: Alberto Jubilini goes further. Protecting everyone is a shared job, and fairness says that each person who can should do their fair share of it.

cb7ed209.text: Notice that this argument works even if one person's choice changes nothing. Leaving your share to others is unfair whether or not anyone is harmed.
cb7ed209.spoken: Notice that this argument works even if one person's choice changes nothing. Leaving your share to others is unfair whether or not anyone is harmed.

e964829d.text: The third argument answers an objection.
e964829d.spoken: The third argument answers an objection.

3aaf561c.text: The objection goes: my one shot makes no difference. Measles spreads or it doesn't, whatever I do.
3aaf561c.spoken: The objection goes: my one shot makes no difference. Measles spreads or it doesn't, whatever I do.

1152634d.text: Jason Brennan, a libertarian philosopher who usually argues against government power, replies with a grim case. A squad of snipers all fire at a child at once. No single shot makes a difference, yet every sniper does wrong.
1152634d.spoken: Jason Brennan, a libertarian philosopher who usually argues against government power, replies with a grim case. A squad of snipers all fire at a child at once. No single shot makes a difference, yet every sniper does wrong.

2c1ce92d.text: His clean hands principle says you have a duty not to take part in collectively harmful activities, and that this duty can sometimes be enforced.
2c1ce92d.spoken: His clean hands principle says you have a duty not to take part in collectively harmful activities, and that this duty can sometimes be enforced.

4acfaf24.text: Staying unvaccinated is joining the group that, together, spreads measles to others. So, Brennan says, stay out of it, even though your part is tiny.
4acfaf24.spoken: Staying unvaccinated is joining the group that, together, spreads measles to others. So, Brennan says, stay out of it, even though your part is tiny.

ca6e146e.text: Many people who agree that vaccines work still object to laws that require them. Here are their strongest reasons.
ca6e146e.spoken: Many people who agree that vaccines work still object to laws that require them. Here are their strongest reasons.

c1d5922b.text: First, bodily integrity. What goes into your body is yours to decide, and a law requiring a medical procedure is a serious step.
c1d5922b.spoken: First, bodily integrity. What goes into your body is yours to decide, and a law requiring a medical procedure is a serious step.

c095e19b.text: Second, parents' rights. Parents normally make medical decisions for their children. Writing in a medical ethics journal in 1999, Peter Bradley argued that this weighs against compulsion where most children are vaccinated anyway.
c095e19b.spoken: Second, parents' rights. Parents normally make medical decisions for their children. Writing in a medical ethics journal in 1999, Peter Bradley argued that this weighs against compulsion where most children are vaccinated anyway.

afbae168.text: Third, conscience. Some families object on religious or moral grounds, and forcing them to act against conscience is a real cost.
afbae168.spoken: Third, conscience. Some families object on religious or moral grounds, and forcing them to act against conscience is a real cost.

faf55b0d.text: And fourth, as little force as possible. The philosopher Mark Navin argues that the state should use only as much coercion as it needs to keep herd immunity.
faf55b0d.spoken: And fourth, as little force as possible. The philosopher Mark Navin argues that the state should use only as much coercion as it needs to keep herd immunity.

The question is how much to do, and how to decide.

7010f627.text: In 2007, the Nuffield Council on Bioethics, a British ethics body, ranked public health policies on a ladder. Higher rungs limit choice more, so they need stronger reasons. From the top. Eliminate choice: vaccinate people against their will. US rules today use fines or exclusion instead. Restrict choice: unvaccinated children stay home during an outbreak. Guide choice through disincentives: a fine, like the five-dollar fine the Supreme Court upheld in 1905. Guide choices through incentives: Ohio's 2021 lottery, with million-dollar prizes for vaccinated adults. Guide choices by changing the default: book flu-shot appointments that people can cancel. Enable choice: free vaccines at school or the pharmacy. Provide information: reminder letters and ad campaigns. And at the bottom, do nothing, or just count the cases. To keep it simple, this lesson groups the rungs above doing nothing into four bands: inform or enable, change the default, incentive or disincentive, and restrict or eliminate choice.

And has it been explained openly to the public?

bffcc06e.text: Being excused from a vaccine law is an old idea too. In 1853, England and Wales made smallpox vaccination compulsory for babies. Protests grew for decades. In 1898, parents who convinced a magistrate that they truly believed vaccination would harm their child were excused. The phrase conscientious objector came into common use in this fight. Today, every US state requires some vaccines for school, and every state excuses children for medical reasons. Most also excuse families who object on religious grounds, and some excuse personal objections too. An exemption excuses someone from a rule. So who should get one?

f935adbc.text: There are three kinds of exemption.
f935adbc.spoken: There are three kinds of exemption.

abe38580.text: Medical. A doctor says the vaccine would be dangerous for this child, for instance because of cancer treatment or a severe allergy.
abe38580.spoken: Medical. A doctor says the vaccine would be dangerous for this child, for instance because of cancer treatment or a severe allergy.

1b7aa472.text: Religious. The family says its faith forbids the vaccine.
1b7aa472.spoken: Religious. The family says its faith forbids the vaccine.

fcecf215.text: Personal belief. The family objects for other reasons of conscience. Some states call this a philosophical exemption.
fcecf215.spoken: Personal belief. The family objects for other reasons of conscience. Some states call this a philosophical exemption.

15f425f8.text: Since 2015, California, New York, Maine, and Connecticut have ended non-medical exemptions. California went first, after the Disneyland outbreak. Courts have reopened the question in Mississippi and West Virginia.
15f425f8.spoken: Since 2015, California, New York, Maine, and Connecticut have ended non-medical exemptions. California went first, after the Disneyland outbreak. Courts have reopened the question in Mississippi and West Virginia.

12788b3d.text: Why should religion get special treatment?
12788b3d.spoken: Why should religion get special treatment?

28786654.text: Many states excuse families who object on religious grounds, but not families with other sincere objections. The philosopher Brian Leiter asks why.
28786654.spoken: Many states excuse families who object on religious grounds, but not families with other sincere objections. The philosopher Brian Lighter asks why.

ec8b7aba.text: He argues there's no good reason to treat religious conscience as more deserving than any other deep conviction.
ec8b7aba.spoken: He argues there's no good reason to treat religious conscience as more deserving than any other deep conviction.

54bf81fc.text: But he doesn't conclude that everyone should be excused. No one, religious or not, should get an exemption that shifts burdens onto other people.
54bf81fc.spoken: But he doesn't conclude that everyone should be excused. No one, religious or not, should get an exemption that shifts burdens onto other people.

135f64d8.text: He names vaccine exemptions as an example. They shift the risk of disease onto other children.
135f64d8.spoken: He names vaccine exemptions as an example. They shift the risk of disease onto other children.

f4f1ddee.text: The philosopher Mark Navin and the historian Mark Largent propose a middle path.
f4f1ddee.spoken: The philosopher Mark Navin and the historian Mark Largent propose a middle path.

74cc2713.text: Keep non-medical exemptions, for religious and secular objectors alike, so families with real convictions aren't forced to act against them.
74cc2713.spoken: Keep non-medical exemptions, for religious and secular objectors alike, so families with real convictions aren't forced to act against them.

6d661b43.text: But make an exemption take effort, like an education session at the health department, plus paperwork. They call this model inconvenience.
6d661b43.spoken: But make an exemption take effort, like an education session at the health department, plus paperwork. They call this model inconvenience.

3c811f93.text: The effort filters out parents who are merely unsure, while sincere objectors can still get an exemption.

5dc7bf6a.text: One last scene from 1853. Esther recovers, but the fever leaves her face scarred. Jo dies. Dickens turns to his readers: Dead, your Majesty. Dead, my lords and gentlemen. Today, vaccines are very safe, but a very small number of people are seriously harmed. Under a 1986 law, a US program pays people harmed by routine vaccines without their having to prove anyone was at fault. The ethicist Ross Upshur's principle of reciprocity covers this. If a community asks you to carry a small risk for everyone's sake, it owes you help if that risk comes due.
